描述_EN: this figure is made of loess, which has fired to the reddish colour visible in places where the glaze has flaked off. the figure has a green lead glaze which has become partly iridescent due to burying. the dog had the task of guarding the tomb and driving away evil influences. the fine texture and low shrinkage rate of loess had made it a favourite raw material for northern chinese pottery. however, it melts at a comparatively low temperature, so if a glaze was required this needed to have an even lower melting point. unless properly prepared, high-lead glazes can poison both makers and users of pots alike. it was made during the eastern han dynasty (ad 25-220) and buried in a grave along with other models of animals, farm buildings and daily vessels according to han funerary customs. modern ceramic historians have been intrigued by this development, as high-lead glazes were also used by roman potters, and one theory, still unsubstantiated, is that the chinese were influenced by the romans. copper oxide, was particularly dangerous as it upset the chemical stability of the glaze and caused lead to leach out. the potters therefore used glazes with a high lead content, which had the advantage of producing brilliant colours with warm tones. this earthenware tomb figure depicts a dog with an upturned tail. these animals, together with architectural models such as watch-towers and water-wells, provide a rich insight into the daily life under the han dynasty (206 bc-ad 220). the silvery iridescence on this dog is partly the result of the unstable glaze, but has been exacerbated by burial conditions and is a characteristic feature of han dynasty green mortuary wares. the chinese tradition of sumptuous burials had led to a great variety of ceramic figures of wild and domesticated animals being interred with the deceased in tombs.
描述_ZN: 此图由黄土制成，在釉面剥落的地方烧成了红色，可见其颜色。 该图有绿色的铅釉，由于被埋葬，部分变成了彩虹色。 狗的任务是守卫坟墓和驱除邪恶的影响。 黄土质地细腻，收缩率低，是中国北方陶器最受欢迎的原料。 然而，它的熔化温度相对较低，所以如果需要釉料，这需要有更低的熔点。 如果没有适当的准备，高铅釉会使制壶者和用壶者都中毒。 它是在东汉时期（公元25-220年）制作的，根据汉代的丧葬习俗，与其他动物、农场建筑和日常器皿的模型一起埋在坟墓里。 现代陶瓷历史学家对这一发展很感兴趣，因为罗马的陶工也使用了高铅釉，有一种理论，至今仍未得到证实，那就是中国人受到了罗马人的影响。 氧化铜特别危险，因为它破坏了釉料的化学稳定性，导致铅的浸出。 因此，陶工们使用了高铅含量的釉料，其优点是可以产生温暖色调的亮丽色彩。 这个陶制墓俑描绘了一只尾巴上翘的狗。 这些动物和建筑模型，如瞭望塔和水井，提供了对汉代（公元前206年-公元220年）日常生活的丰富洞察力。 这只狗身上的银色虹彩部分是由不稳定的釉料造成的，但由于埋藏条件而加剧，是汉代绿色殡仪馆的一个特征。 中国传统的奢华葬礼导致了大量的野生和驯养动物的陶瓷形象与死者一起被埋葬在坟墓中。
